full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury, J: This petition calls in question the judgment and order of the High Court Division passed in Criminal Misc. Case No 4122 of 1997 under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure refusing to quash the judgment and order of the Special Tribunal, Chittagong, in Special Tribunal Case 'No. 116 of 1993, convicting the petitioner under Section 376 of the Penal Code read with the Special Powers Act, 1974 and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and to pay a fine of Tk. 5000/- in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more for having committed rape upon P.W. 1 Salina Khatun. 

 3. In support of the case the prosecution examined 5 witnesses, of whom P.W. 1 Salina Khatun is the victim herself, P.W. 2 Nurul Islam is her brother and P.W. 3 and P.W. 4 are the two doctors who examined the victim. P.W. 5 is the Investigating Officer. 

 5. The petitioner thereupon filed Criminal Misc. Case No. 4122 of 1997 for quashment of his conviction and sentence. After hearing the parties the learned Judges of the High Court Division held that the prosecutrix was sufficiently corroborated by her brother, P.W. 2 and the medical evidence, Ext. 3, the discharge certificate of the hospital as a ground for discharge of the Rule. 

 6. To this view we entirely agree. But the learned Judges of the High Court Division in course of their judgment ventilated the view that there is no necessity of a prosecutrix being corroborated by other evidence for warranting conviction. To quote them "under Section 118 of the Evidence Act a prosecutrix, who is the victim of rape or sexual offence, is undoubtedly a competent witness and she is entitled to receive the same weight as is attached to an injured person in case of physical violence". We are unable to agree. The position of a prosecutrix is a little different from that of an injured person simpliciter. The possibility of a prosecutrix being a collaborator cannot always be ruled out. Therefore a corroboration of the evidence of prosecutrix by at least some circumstantial evidence or a medical examination is always desirable.
